name: Hatfield Safety Squat Bar Squat
description: A squat performed with a safety squat bar while the hands brace against the upright posts of a power rack. The rack contact eliminates balance demands, allowing higher training intensities or deeper ranges of motion. The SSB's camber promotes an upright torso naturally, making this a useful tool for athletes with shoulder or wrist mobility restrictions.

execution.starting_position: Stand inside a power rack with the safety squat bar on your upper back. Grip the rack uprights at a comfortable height with both hands.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the SSB in the rack at the correct height. Load the bar. Stand inside the rack and grip the uprights before unracking.
steps: Step 1: Brace your core and unrack the bar, gripping the uprights lightly.
Step 2: Descend into a squat while keeping hands lightly on the rack uprights for balance — do not press off the rack to aid the ascent.
Step 3: Reach depth (at or below parallel) with an upright torso.
Step 4: Drive through the heels to return to standing.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before descent. Exhale during the ascent.
common_mistakes: Pressing hard off the rack uprights to cheat the ascent
Excessive forward lean due to overloading
safety_considerations: Use the uprights only for balance — pressing off them turns this into an assisted exercise rather than a true squat
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Squat to at least parallel. The SSB's camber angle naturally encourages an upright torso.
coaching_cues: Use the rack for balance only, not assistance
